status-warning.note: Darkened from a #b98900 first-pass value that read 2.8:1 on its badge background, below the AA 4.5:1 floor.

title.purpose: Section h2/h3 inside a panel or dialog.

label.purpose: Field labels, nav items, button text.

shadows.name: hairline-lift
shadows.purpose: Auth card and modal dialog only; every other surface is flat.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action on a view; the only routine spend of the amber accent besides live/active nav state.
components.css: .ds-btn { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; min-height: 40px; line-height: 1; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, border-color 150ms ease-out, color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary { background: #a8560a; border-color: #a8560a; color: #ffffff; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #8c4708; border-color: #8c4708; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #a8560a; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default button everywhere a primary action isn't called for; deliberately ink, not amber.

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Outlined, transparent-background destructive action (e.g. Divisions screen Delete).

components.name: Text Input
components.css: .ds-input { font-size: 1rem; color: #211e19; background: #faf7f1; border: 1px solid #c9bfa9; border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; min-height: 40px; } .ds-input:hover { border-color: #8a8372; } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: #a8560a; outline: none; }

components.name: Warning Badge
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; padding: 2px 0.5rem; border-radius: 4px; line-height: 1.6; } .ds-badge-warning { background: #faf1d9; color: #8a6300; }

components.name: Panel
components.description: The primary content container; flat at rest, no shadow.

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: Left-rail nav link; active state marked by amber text plus an inset hairline, not a filled background.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: block; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 6px; color: #5b5548; text-decoration: none; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: #ffffff; color: #211e19; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: #ffffff; color: #a8560a; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #e1dacb; }

narrative.overview:
This is the meet-day operations desk, not a broadcast scoreboard. It refuses the flashy jumbotron/LED-scoreboard default that most "competition software" briefs reach for, in favor of the one trustworthy laminated clipboard at the check-in table: plain, dense, and legible under gym lighting. Warm off-white paper carries near-black ink text; a single marker/highlighter amber accent is spent only on primary actions and live/active state, never on decoration, links, or secondary buttons. The system-default sans is used throughout -- no display face, no serif accent -- because the tool's job is to disappear behind the data it holds.

An organizer scans a dense list, finds the one thing needing action, acts, and trusts the result saved. Nothing else competes for attention: no gradients, no drop shadows beyond a 1px hairline lift on the few genuinely floating surfaces (auth card, modal dialog), and radius is small and consistent (4-6px) rather than either sharp-cornered or bubbly.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground + near-black ink + one reserved amber accent
One system-stack sans, tabular numerals on every numeric/data column
Hairline (1px) borders and dividers; radius capped at 6px, never 0
Flat at rest; shadow is reserved for two floating surfaces only (auth card, dialog)
Left-rail nav on desktop, collapsing to a horizontal scroll strip under 720px

rules.name: The Reserved Amber Rule
rules.body: The accent exists in exactly one place per screen at most: the primary action or the thing that's live/active right now. It never appears on a link, a secondary or danger button, or as a decorative fill -- an earlier draft spent it on plain links and a secondary button and was corrected before ship.

rules.name: The AA Floor Rule
rules.body: Every text-on-background and control-on-background pairing that carries meaning clears 4.5:1. Two colors in this palette (marker-amber, status-warning) were darkened from their first-pass values specifically to clear this floor; the darkened values are the system, not the drafts.

rules.name: The One Stack Rule
rules.body: No second (display or serif) font family exists anywhere in the shipped app. Headings are the same sans as body text, distinguished only by weight (650) and size.

rules.name: The Hairline-Only Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs to read as "above" the page, the border gets a 1px hairline shadow -- nothing softer, nothing larger, and nothing on a surface that's just sitting in-flow.

dos: Do reserve marker amber for the primary action and live/active state only (The Reserved Amber Rule).
Do apply tabular-nums to every numeric column, badge, or timestamp.
Do cap radius at 6px on containers and 4px on small elements nested inside them; never 0.
Do confirm any new color pairing clears 4.5:1 contrast before shipping (The AA Floor Rule) -- this system has already had to correct two colors for this once.
donts: Don't use a gradient anywhere in the UI.
Don't add a shadow to a panel, card, list row, or badge sitting in normal document flow -- shadow is reserved for the auth card and the dialog only.
Don't spend the amber accent on a plain link or a secondary/tertiary button; links and secondary buttons stay ink-colored.
Don't introduce a second font family (display or serif) for headings or any other role.
